import AppKit

/// One sub-tab of the Clip tab (spec §11 CI-5). The case order is the display
/// order: Text and Shape come first for those kinds, Clip is always last.
enum ClipSubTab: String, CaseIterable {
    case text, shape, graphic, picture, color, sound, clip

    var title: String {
        switch self {
        case .text: return "Text"
        case .shape: return "Shape"
        case .graphic: return "Graphic"
        case .picture: return "Picture"
        case .color: return "Color"
        case .sound: return "Sound"
        case .clip: return "Clip"
        }
    }

    /// The `◆N` badge (spec §11 CI-6): how many KEYS of an action's end patch
    /// this tab's sections write. Motion lives on Clip, so Picture counts the
    /// video keys without it; a shape's props are not animatable; Graphic
    /// counts the end's `graphic.props`, a key its module no longer declares
    /// included (CI-6 amended, G-34 (l)). Color counts `color`, one key
    /// however many of its thirteen the end names, and Picture no longer does
    /// (CI-6 amended by GR-2); for an all-adjustment selection (`adjustment`)
    /// it also counts `opacity`, the Adjustment section's Strength (GR-6). An
    /// end's `look` is Color's too, one key (GR-7), and so is its `wheels`,
    /// one key however many of its nine it names (GR-11), and its `curves`,
    /// one key however many channels it names (GR-12), and its `qualifier`,
    /// one key however many ranges it names (GR-13); Picture counts none of
    /// them. Clip also counts an end's `speed`, the Speed section's Rate (CI-6
    /// amended by SR-21).
    func keyedCount(in end: ActionPatch, adjustment: Bool = false) -> Int {
        switch self {
        case .text: return end.text?.dictionary.count ?? 0
        case .shape: return 0
        case .graphic: return end.graphic?.props.count ?? 0
        case .picture:
            let other: Set<String> = ["motion", "color", "look", "wheels", "curves", "qualifier"]
            return end.video?.dictionary.keys.filter { !other.contains($0) }.count ?? 0
        case .color:
            return (end.video?.color?.isEmpty == false ? 1 : 0)
                + (end.video?.dictionary["look"] != nil ? 1 : 0)
                + (end.video?.wheels?.isEmpty == false ? 1 : 0)
                + (end.video?.curves?.isEmpty == false ? 1 : 0)
                + (end.video?.qualifier?.isEmpty == false ? 1 : 0)
                + (adjustment && end.video?.dictionary["opacity"] != nil ? 1 : 0)
        case .sound: return end.audio?.dictionary.count ?? 0
        case .clip:
            return (end.video?.dictionary["motion"] == nil ? 0 : 1) + (end.speed == nil ? 0 : 1)
        }
    }
}

/// The strip of sub-tabs under the action lane: equal square cells whose 1 pt
/// borders collapse into one, the active cell in the selection fill with an
/// accent border, and a mint `◆N` after a label whose tab the selected action
/// keys. Built with its tabs and its active one, like `PanelTabsView`: a pick
/// goes out through `onSelect` and the pane is rebuilt with a new strip.
/// No hover — a mode switch is instant.
final class ClipSubTabsView: NSView, OptionControl {
    static let cell: CGFloat = 24, top: CGFloat = 8, bottom: CGFloat = 8
    private static let side = InspectorMetrics.inset

    let tabs: [ClipSubTab]
    let active: ClipSubTab
    private let badge: (ClipSubTab) -> Int
    private let onSelect: (ClipSubTab) -> Void
    private var badges: [Int] = []

    init(
        tabs: [ClipSubTab], active: ClipSubTab, badge: @escaping (ClipSubTab) -> Int,
        onSelect: @escaping (ClipSubTab) -> Void
    ) {
-----
## `set_action`

Moves an action, changes its length or changes its easing curve. It mirrors the selected action's start, length and curve controls in the Clip tab's action lane, and dragging a band. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
| `start` | integer | No | The new start, in clip time. |
| `duration` | integer | No | The new length. |
| `curve` | string | No | How the values ease: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

Give at least one of `start`, `duration` and `curve`. Any you leave out keep their value.

**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action's end names a speed, captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).

**When it refuses.**

- It would overlap another action on the clip.
- It would end past the clip's end and later than it ended before. An action a trim left past the clip's end can still be re-curved, moved earlier or shortened.
- On a speed action, it would make the clip read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
- On a speed action of a linked clip, it would change the clip's speed: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
- With none of the three arguments, the call answers "set_action needs start, duration or curve."

## `set_action_end`

Sets what an action animates to. It mirrors every inspector field written while an action is selected. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) and [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The end state, with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`. |
| `off` | array of strings | No | `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end. See [Switching off at an end](#switching-off-at-an-end). |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "opacity": 0 }, "audio": { "volume": 0.2 } } }
```

The patch merges into the end state key by key, at every depth, so a one-key `shadow` keeps the rest of it. A key set to `null` is removed from the end state, so that property stops being animated, and a group set to `null` removes the whole group.

The `video`, `audio` and `text` groups take the same keys as [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/), [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) and [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/). A colour is four numbers here too, and it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha. So do the chroma key's three numbers.

A bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it, such as `video.filters[1].kind`. Values aren't range-checked, though: an animation can aim past what a stored property could hold.

**Sound.** Every key the sound's effects read animates: `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation`, beside `volume` and the fades.

- Numbers ramp.
- A switch changes when the action ends: a group or an EQ slot turned on, `mono`, `channels`, an EQ slope, hum's frequency and harmonics, and the leveller's response.
- `isolation` ramps from 0 on a clip with none.
- `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` are stored but never animate.

See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).

**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. With `speed` in the patch it can add the keys listed under [Speed in an action](#speed-in-an-action).

**When it refuses.** These keys are errors, a `null` included:

| Key | Why, and what to do instead |
| --- | --- |
| `video.motion` | It's a preset tied to the clip's two ends. Set it with `set_video`. |
| `video.hide_silent` | It isn't an animation target. Set it with `set_video`. |
| `text.words` | Word times belong to speech. Set them with `set_text`. |
| `video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality` | They're the clip's own. Set them with `set_video`. A cutout's `edge`, `feather` and `background` do animate. |
| Any `shape` key | Shapes can't be animated, so `shape` isn't a group here. |

### Animating graphic props

A graphic clip's props are a fourth group: `graphic: {props: {<key>: <value>}}`, keyed by what its module declares. It mirrors the Graphic sub-tab's **Properties** with an action selected. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

```json
{ "clip": 18, "action": 44, "patch": { "graphic": { "props": { "accent": "#ff5500", "count": 96 } } } }
```

- A value is checked as `set_graphic` checks it, minimum and maximum included, against the module as the project's graphics folder holds it now.
- A number ramps along the curve and arrives with decimals, so 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway. A module that needs a whole number rounds it.
- A colour blends in OKLab, with straight alpha.
- A string, a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ends.
- An image prop switches when the action ends. `""` names no image there.
- A prop the clip holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into the clip in the same undo step.
- `graphic.props.<key>: null` removes that prop from the end, and `graphic: null` removes the whole group.

`get_project` shows `kinds` beside `props`. Frame Job writes that and ignores any you send, so an end you read back can be sent again.

**When it refuses.**

- A prop its module marks `animate: false` is refused. Set it with `set_graphic`.
- `name`, `width`, `height`, `in` and `length` are refused: an action animates `graphic.props` only.
- While the module is missing or doesn't compile, a value is refused, and `get_graphic` says why. A `null` still removes.
- On a clip that isn't a graphic: "clip 7 is not a graphic clip".

### Speed in an action

`speed`, a number beside the groups, is a media clip's rate. The clip ramps from the rate in force to it along the curve and holds it after, and it keeps its start and length, playing more or less source. It mirrors the Speed section's **Rate** with an action selected. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "speed": 3 } }
```

The rate is clamped to ×0.1–×1000, and `speed: null` removes it.

Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the call that takes it there answers with `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note`. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays.

**When it refuses.**

- An end rate that would read past the end of the clip's media. The sentence names the largest end rate that fits, or, when none down to ×0.1 does, the latest clip end that fits at ×0.1.
- `speed: null` when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
- A value that isn't a number or `null`, or a clip that isn't a media clip.
- A rate on a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".

### Switching off at an end

`off` turns an optional property off at the end of the action. The path is stored as a `null` in the end state, where a `null` in `patch` removes the key instead. So `off` means "this shadow goes away by the end", and a `null` in `patch` means "stop animating the shadow".

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": {}, "off": ["video.shadow", "audio.eq.band_2"] }
```

- A path is `"group.key"`, with a group of `video`, `audio` or `text` and one of its top-level keys, such as `video.shadow`, `text.width` or `audio.limiter`.
- One deeper path exists: `audio.eq.<slot>` switches that EQ slot off. The slots are `high_pass`, `low_shelf`, `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3`, `high_shelf` and `low_pass`.
- Only optional keys can go off. A required key such as `video.opacity` is refused.
- A path can't also be named in `patch`.
- `graphic` paths are refused: name the value a prop ends at in `patch`.
- `video.cutout` is refused: `set_video` with `{cutout: null}` removes a cutout.
- `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent` and `text.words` are refused here too.

## `remove_action`

Removes an action. The clip keeps its base properties. It mirrors the action lane's trash button and <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an action selected. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action named a speed, captions are re-timed in the same step, with `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` as for `set_action`.

**When it refuses.**

- Removing a speed action when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
- Removing a speed action from a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
- An action id the clip doesn't have is an error.

## Related

/// The two refusals that are about this op rather than the vocabulary,
/// asked of a group and a key wherever they came from — a `patch`'s keys
/// and an `off` path go through the same two sentences. The third arm is
/// `off`'s alone: a cutout's presence is the clip's own (spec §11 CO-20),
/// so an end may not take it away; a `patch` naming `video.cutout` is
/// [`check_cutout_end`]'s.
pub(crate) fn not_a_target(group: &str, key: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    match (group, key) {
        ("video", "motion") => Err("video.motion is not an animation target".to_string()),
        ("video", "hide_silent") => Err("video.hide_silent is not an animation target".to_string()),
        ("text", "words") => Err("text.words is not an animation target".to_string()),
        ("video", "cutout") => Err("video.cutout cannot be keyed off at an action's end; \
                                    set_video {cutout: null} removes it"
            .to_string()),
        _ => Ok(()),
    }
}

/// A `patch`'s `video.cutout` naming `subject` or `quality` — a `null`
/// included, `subject` asked first — refused by name (spec §11 CO-20): which
/// subject and which masks are the clip's own, and the evaluator restores
/// the base's over any end (`cutout_check.rs`'s `restore_base_cutout`).
/// `edge`, `feather` and `background` pass; anything that is not an object
/// is the walk's to judge.
pub(crate) fn check_cutout_end(patch: &Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    let Some(Value::Object(cutout)) = patch.get("video").and_then(|video| video.get("cutout"))
    else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    for key in ["subject", "quality"] {
        if cutout.contains_key(key) {
            return Err(format!("video.cutout.{key} is not an animation target"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

| Hatching | At the clip's start, as long as the overlap | The clip has a [transition](/motion/transitions/) and overlaps the clip before it. |
| Fades | Triangles along the bottom, at either end | The clip has sound and a fade in or out. |
| Motion wedges | Triangles hanging from the top, at either end | The clip has an active In or Out [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/). |

### Detail row

This row appears only while an action is selected. Its fields have no labels, so read them from left to right as they're listed here. Each change is one undo step.

| Control | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Where the action starts, as a timecode measured from the clip's own start. | |
| Length | How long the action takes, in seconds, snapped to whole frames. | 0.01 to 36,000 s, with quick picks of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2. A longer value is held to the clip's length. |
| Curve | How the action eases from its start to its end state, with a glyph of the curve beside it. | Linear, In, Out, In Out |
| Trash button | Removes the action. <kbd>⌫</kbd> does the same. | |

If Frame Job can't take a typed Start or Length, for example because the action would overlap another or run past the clip's end, it beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused:". The line stays until the project next changes or you click it.

### Several clips selected

With several clips selected the lane reads "Select one clip to edit its actions.", and there's no count, Clip chip, bands or detail row.

- A detail row appears with the action's start, length, curve and trash button.

## The Clip chip

The **Clip** chip sits at the start of the action lane. It's highlighted while no action is selected, which tells you the fields edit the clip. Click it while an action is selected to leave the action.

## Leave an action

Do any of these, and the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again:

- Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.
- Click the **Clip** chip.
- Select a different clip.

Moving the playhead out of the span doesn't leave the action. It stays selected, and the fields keep editing its end state.

After <kbd>Esc</kbd> or the **Clip** chip, the playhead can stay inside the span without selecting the action again. It's selected the next time the playhead leaves and comes back.

With no action selected, <kbd>Esc</kbd> does whatever it would do otherwise.

38:## Speech the clip no longer plays
42:A caption whose speech the clip no longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that's only partly reached keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.
50:A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a caption that didn't move. One that would start inside such a caption, or end up shorter than a frame, is removed.
60:`set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_action`, `remove_action` and `set_action_end` re-time captions the same way, in the same undo step. `set_action_end` does so only when it changes the speed.
62:The result lists the caption clips that moved in `captions_retimed` and the ones removed in `captions_removed`. Each key appears only when it has something in it. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/) and [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
74:| Content | | The words |
84:A word caption page's timing can't animate, because it belongs to the speech. There's no inspector section for its word colours and pop scale, so only an agent can put those in an action. They ramp when it does. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
111:- **Picture sub-tab:** the [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) section, **Remove background**, **Subject** and the header's **Reset** (which carries no mark) in the Background section, and **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** in the Cursor section.
122:This covers the shadow, chroma key, text, outline, backdrop, word caption and graphic colours. Opacity moves separately from the colour. A colour whose two ends are equal stays exact all the way through, and there's no setting for any of this.
130:Frame Job won't accept the keys that belong to the clip: `video.motion`, `text.words`, `video.cutout.subject` and `video.cutout.quality`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
